title: Helm: add backup CronJob + restore Job primitives with safe concurrency controls
creator: Talia Benson
links: GitHub: redwood-helm-charts PR #433 (scheduled backups + one-shot restore jobs)
GitHub: redwood-private-installer PR #901 (maintenance mode toggles during restore)
description:
Goal
- Provide Helm chart primitives for Redwood Private operators to run (a) scheduled backups and (b) one-shot restore execution, with guardrails to prevent overlapping backups and to reduce DB contention.

Scope
- Helm templates + values for:
  1) Backup CronJob (scheduled) that runs `rw-private-dr backup create` and emits structured logs/metrics.
  2) Backup verify Job (optional on schedule / or post-backup hook) that runs `rw-private-dr backup verify`.
  3) Restore Job (manual, one-shot) that runs `rw-private-dr restore execute` with prechecks and validation gates.
- Safe concurrency controls (do not allow multiple backup jobs to run simultaneously; do not allow restore to run while backup is active).
- Resource guidance and operational knobs (timeouts, retry policies, backup windows).

Non-goals
- Building a full UI/workflow in Console for scheduling (operators control via Helm values / GitOps).
- Handling custom backup implementations outside the CLI interface.

Design notes / constraints
- Must work in restricted networks (private subnets and on-prem).
- Must integrate cleanly with service accounts / customer IAM (IRSA/workload identity patterns), without hardcoding cloud-specific assumptions.
- Must be safe under upgrades/rollbacks (CronJob should be suspendable; restore Job should be explicit/manual).
- Keep chart changes backwards-compatible for existing Private installs (feature flags default off or non-invasive defaults).

Implementation plan
1) Chart values + templating
- Add values under `privateDr.*` (naming final TBD per docs):
  - `privateDr.backup.enabled` (default: false)
  - `privateDr.backup.schedule` (cron string)
  - `privateDr.backup.suspend` (default: false)
  - `privateDr.backup.concurrencyPolicy` (default: Forbid)
  - `privateDr.backup.startingDeadlineSeconds` (default: 600)
  - `privateDr.backup.activeDeadlineSeconds` (default: 14400) to prevent "stuck for 2h" jobs running indefinitely
  - `privateDr.backup.backoffLimit` (default: 1)
  - `privateDr.backup.resources` (requests/limits)
  - `privateDr.backup.nodeSelector/tolerations/affinity` (optional)
  - `privateDr.backup.env` + `extraEnvFrom` for storage/KMS wiring
  - `privateDr.backup.secretMounts` for credentials (where customers do not use cloud identity)
  - `privateDr.restore.enabled` (default: false; Job template exists but not installed unless enabled)
  - `privateDr.restore.jobAnnotations` to support change-management evidence (ticket ids, approver)

2) Concurrency / safety controls
- For CronJob:
  - Use `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` and `successfulJobsHistoryLimit` / `failedJobsHistoryLimit` to reduce clutter.
  - Set `startingDeadlineSeconds` and `activeDeadlineSeconds` to keep the scheduler from creating overlapping jobs after missed windows.
- Cluster-level guardrails:
  - Add a lightweight "lock" via Kubernetes Lease (preferred) or ConfigMap-based lock (fallback) so that:
    - Backup job exits early (non-zero) if another backup is active.
    - Restore job exits early (non-zero) if a backup lock is held.
  - Ensure lock includes identity (pod name, start time) and TTL behavior to avoid permanent lock if a node dies.
- PDB / scheduling guidance:
  - Add PodDisruptionBudget for control-plane DB dependent components if not already present (PR #447) and document that backup should run off-peak.

3) Restore Job behavior
- Restore should be explicit/manual:
  - Provide `helm template` and documented `helm upgrade --set privateDr.restore.enabled=true` flow (or separate chart values file) rather than automatic creation.
  - Restore Job should set/require maintenance mode before performing DB restore steps (coordination with ENG-4904 / PR #901).

4) Observability hooks (interface only)
- Ensure job names/labels are stable for dashboards:
  - Labels: `app.kubernetes.io/component=private-dr`, `redwood.ai/dr-operation=backup|restore`, `redwood.ai/cluster-id` where available.
  - Provide runbook URL annotation pattern on CronJob/Job templates (observability tooling will scrape/attach).

Acceptance criteria
- Backup CronJob can be enabled with a single values block and renders valid manifests with `helm template`.
- Backup CronJob defaults prevent overlapping execution (CronJob `Forbid` + lock).
- Restore Job template is present and can be enabled manually; it fails fast if backup is running.
- All jobs run with a configurable ServiceAccount (no default cluster-admin assumptions).
- Operators can configure timeouts/retries, backup windows, and resource requests/limits.
- Documentation snippet (values example + operational notes) included in chart README / release notes.

Test plan
- Template/render validation:
  - `helm lint` on chart.
  - `helm template` golden output checks for the following configurations:
    1) backup enabled / restore disabled
    2) backup disabled / restore enabled
    3) backup enabled with secret mounts
- Unit tests (helm-unittest or chart-testing):
  - Assert `concurrencyPolicy=Forbid` by default when backup enabled.
  - Assert Job/CronJob have expected labels/annotations.
  - Assert ServiceAccount name is configurable and referenced correctly.
- Integration smoke (CI Kind cluster):
  - Deploy chart with backup enabled and short schedule (e.g., every 2 minutes) and validate:
    - At most one backup pod runs at a time.
    - A second scheduled run during an active backup is skipped/blocked.
  - Trigger restore job while backup is active and validate restore job exits early with actionable logs.
  - Trigger restore job when backup is not active and validate it reaches the first "precheck" stage (we don’t need a full restore to pass this ticket; full restore validation tracked in ENG-4848/ENG-4904).

Rollout / release notes
- Gate behind values `privateDr.backup.enabled` and `privateDr.restore.enabled` (default false).
- Add a short upgrade note: if operators are already running bespoke backup CronJobs, do not enable Redwood-provided schedule until they’ve migrated storage/IAM wiring.

Risks / open questions
- Lock implementation choice: Lease API requires RBAC permissions; fallback to ConfigMap lock if customer policy disallows Leases. Prefer Lease for better semantics.
- Timeouts: defaults need to be conservative for large artifact stores; ensure activeDeadlineSeconds is configurable and documented.
- Naming: Align with Docs IA (docs thread suggested "Day-2 ops" grouping).
comments: 2025-10-10 (Diego Santos): Drafted values schema and templates for backup CronJob + restore Job. Waiting on final CLI container image tag strategy from Connor (versioned tooling).

2025-10-18 (Allison Grant): Please ensure labels include `redwood.ai/dr-operation` and that Job names are stable for dashboard queries. Also add runbook link annotation convention (`redwood.ai/runbook-url`).

2025-10-29 (Rafael Mendes): ConcurrencyPolicy=Forbid helps but we still need a cross-job lock. We hit overlapping backups in a missed-window scenario during a drill (cron catch-up). +1 to Lease/TTL lock.

2025-11-06 (Diego Santos): Implemented Lease-based lock with ConfigMap fallback. Added activeDeadlineSeconds + startingDeadlineSeconds defaults. Open PRs: #433 (core templates) + #447 (PDB/concurrency) + #452 (timeouts/retries values).
2025-11-20 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure restore fails fast if backup lock held, and that error message includes next steps ("check rw-private-dr /backup-status" and the runbook link).
